correctness.rationale: Simplex KKT gives P_r(x)_i=(x_i-tau)_+, and each nonempty support S of size k occurs on a strict open affine cell. Its Jacobian is mean-centering on S and zero outside, annihilating constants. Coarea shows its induced complete-pair Gini norm is maximized by a binary cut T. If a=|S∩T|, b=k-a, c=n-k and u=|T\S|, the output has values b/k, -a/k, 0 with exact dispersion ab(1+2c/k), and the input has (a+u)(b+c-u). Concavity of the denominator in u makes an endpoint optimal; monotonicity in the smaller active group gives a=1, b=k-1. The resulting support norm (k-1)(2n-k)/(k(n-1)) is attained by one-coordinate perturbations inside its strict cell. The forward difference -1+2n/[k(k+1)] proves the exact maximizing support inequalities and the asymptotic 2-2sqrt(2/n)+O(1/n). Fixed-input contraction is a separate 1-Lipschitz threshold map statement. Independently enumerated all 2..8 support subsets and proper binary cuts with exact fractions, recovering every claimed finite n norm.

evidence: Duchi/Condat simplex algorithms and the sparsemax active Jacobian provide the KKT structure. A known Jacobian does not determine its induced norm in all-pair Gini variation without separate coarea and cardinality optimization.

value.rationale: Simplex projection is ubiquitous in optimization and sparse probability transformations. The contrast between fixed-input dispersion contraction and two-input expansion, the precise first dimension, the optimal active support near sqrt(2n) and the approach to factor 2 quantify a genuine and useful perturbation-stability gap in a natural seminorm. The all-dimensional classification is stronger than a routine KKT restatement.
